translation_notes: all OWL_NS.<x> reads become owl:<x> islands, in every operand position the region uses: the argument of set(), the elements of a list display passed to .difference(), the left operand of an 'in' test (owl:Restriction in cls.type) and a list display inside the tuple given to triples_choices
OWL_NS = Namespace(...) is absorbed by '@prefix owl: ...'; nothing else needed it as a runtime object

the upstream bug set(OWL_NS.resourceProperties) - iterating a URIRef yields its characters, so CLASS_RELATIONS is a 22-element set of single characters - is preserved verbatim: set(owl:resourceProperties) produces exactly the same set on both sides (checked)

the mechanical draft named the prefix after the Python variable ('owl-ns:') and inserted the @prefix block inside the parenthesised 'from rdflib import (' list; both are invalid ldpy (a hyphenated prefix is silently left as-is in expression position, giving invalid Python), so the prefix was renamed owl: and the declarations moved before the imports
'from rdflib import (...)' left untouched though Namespace/RDF/RDFS are no longer needed by the region itself - same convention as the sibling region AllClasses

context shim: infixowl_shim.py re-exports BooleanClass, CastClass, Class, Individual, Restriction and classOrIdentifier from rdflib 7.2.1's rdflib.extras.infixowl (the maintained descendant of the vendored file, which targets rdflib 3.x and no longer imports); identical on both sides

demo harness added identically to both sides: ComponentTerms is a generator, so the demo builds a small OWL graph covering its three branches (named superclass + anonymous someValuesFrom restriction, owl:unionOf BooleanClass, leaf class) and prints the identifiers; demo_graph is compared by isomorphism, the three printed lines by stdout equality
